chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Whoever gives justification for an unjust one for his injustice, Allah will cause the one who would oppress him to overpower him; so if he supplicates, it will not be answered for him, and Allah will not recompense him for his being oppressed.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of justifying an unjust person's actions?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes the principle of 'justification of the oppressor' (ta'thir al-zalim), warning that passive complicity or verbal endorsement of injustice incurs divine retribution. It highlights that Allah will appoint a new oppressor to the justifier, rendering their supplications ineffective and denying them reward for their own suffering, thereby linking social justice directly to individual spiritual accountability.
